title: Polish Future Tense: Będę, Zrobię and When to Use Each
excerpt: The Polish future tense made simple: będę + verb for ongoing actions, perfective forms like zrobię for results, plus plans, mistakes and practice.
metaDescription: The Polish future tense made simple: będę + verb for ongoing actions, perfective forms like zrobię for results, plus plans, mistakes and practice.
summary: Imperfective verbs form the Polish future with będę, będziesz, będzie, będziemy, będziecie, będą plus either the infinitive (będę robić) or the -ł form (będę robił/robiła).
Perfective verbs have no present tense: their present-style conjugation is the future, so zrobię means 'I will do it'.
Będę never combines with a perfective verb, so 'będę zrobić' is always wrong.
For plans, Polish also uses mieć zamiar, zamierzać, or the plain present tense with a time word (Jutro jadę do Krakowa).

factNotes: All conjugated forms were checked against en.wiktionary.org conjugation tables, which list both compound-future variants (będę robić / będę robił) side by side. The tip that speakers often prefer the -ł form before a second infinitive (będę musiał wstać) is hedged as 'many speakers prefer' and 'both occur', because I could not open a Poradnia PWN entry confirming it. The claim that musieć, móc and chcieć have no perfective partner is hedged as 'no everyday perfective partner', because zechcieć exists. No statistics, dates or quotes are used. Stock images are generic and are not claimed to be Polish. The post links /blog/polish-past-tense (scheduled 2026-11-17, before this post's 2026-12-11 date).
